Brown/Lamar/…, and the top-25 median rank delta against the board's own ordering falls **55 slots → 21**. **That comparison was rigged: it measured the two candidate currencies against EACH OTHER, which cannot say which is closer to the ordering the tool already trusts.** The neutral test is each against `vorp`, and it REVERSES on every decision-relevant subset (window ADP≤160, K/DEF excluded; % = cross-position pairs disagreeing with VORP): **all pairs 33.5% → 32.0%** · **a QB on one side 51.6% → 42.0% (better)** · **within 20 ADP of each other 40.1% → 41.8% (WORSE)** · a QB on one side AND within 20 ADP 31.9% → 33.1% (WORSE) · **NO QB either side, the control, 22.8% → 26.1% (WORSE)**. **Re-pricing wins only on the aggregate QB set, which is dominated by pairs nobody weighs against each other — an elite QB against a fringe receiver. Restricted to players Cory could actually choose between it LOSES, and it damages the RB-vs-WR comparison he will mostly use in order to repair the QB one.** **Mechanism, from the formula itself: `boom = ceiling − mean` is replacement-INVARIANT — `(ceil−R)−(mean−R)` is `ceil−mean` — so a level subtraction fixes only the mean half, and near replacement `max(0, mean−R)` collapses toward zero and hands the ranking to a boom term still denominated in raw points, where a QB's absolute spread is ~2× a receiver's. A real fix must re-denominate boom too: a value-model change, not a four-line patch, and not something to attempt four days out.** **SO THE RECOMMENDATION HARDENS TO: REFUSE, NEVER RE-PRICE** — and §6 of the test pins that, with the instruction to keep it even after the refusal ships, because the re-pricing idea will occur to the next reader exactly as it occurred to me.
